problem_statement: When CONFIG_SMP_CALL is enabled, an application that includes nuttx/sched.h and calls nxsched_smp_call_single or nxsched_smp_call sees those interfaces as absent and the build fails. The kernel lacks the SMP function-call feature. For SMP systems, the scheduler should provide nxsched_smp_call_single and nxsched_smp_call. nxsched_smp_call_single should ask one specified CPU to execute a callback, while nxsched_smp_call should ask every CPU in the supplied cpu_set_t to execute the same callback. Each callback receives a single FAR void * argument and returns an int. The wait argument should control completion semantics: with false, the request should be delivered to the target CPU(s) and the API should return without requiring the callback to have completed, allowing the caller to synchronize later on an external side effect; with true, the API should not return until every targeted callback has completed, and should report an error if any callback returns a negative result. If the target set includes the current CPU, that callback should execute before the caller waits for remote targets. The executed callback must not perform waiting or blocking operations. The feature should be guarded by CONFIG_SMP_CALL and available on supported SMP configurations.

superseded_statements.problem_statement: The test smp_call.c calls nxsched_smp_call_single() and nxsched_smp_call() to dispatch callback functions to specific CPUs via IPI, verifying semaphore signaling in both wait and nowait modes. These kernel APIs do not exist in the old kernel, causing a compile/link failure. The test needs CONFIG_SMP_CALL enabled and an arch-specific up_send_smp_call() implementation to deliver inter-processor interrupts.

superseded_statements.problem_statement: With the apps-side ostest change applied, enabling CONFIG_SMP_CALL causes the ostest build to include smp_call.c and call smp_call_test from ostest_main. Against the base kernel, this fails to build: smp_call.c:64:7 gives an implicit-declaration error for nxsched_smp_call_single, and the related nxsched_smp_call interface is also unavailable. The new test expects a kernel-provided SMP function-call API, gated by CONFIG_SMP_CALL, that allows a caller to request a callback to run on another core or on a set of cores. The test calls nxsched_smp_call_single for each configured CPU and nxsched_smp_call for a CPU set obtained from sched_getaffinity(0). The callback posts a semaphore; the caller then uses sem_wait and sem_getvalue to verify completion. The required behavior is that nxsched_smp_call_single targets one CPU and nxsched_smp_call targets the supplied cpu_set_t. When wait=false, the call should return without blocking while the callback still executes on the target CPU(s). When wait=true, the call should return only after all targeted CPU(s) have completed the callback. If the target set includes the current CPU, the callback may execute locally; if no remote target remains after local execution, the call should still return normally for both wait and non-wait cases and must not cause the test to hang. A non-OK callback result should be observable to a waiting caller. The result should be that ostest smp_call_test builds and passes on qemu-armv8a:nsh_smp with CONFIG_SMP_CALL, including a single-CPU SMP configuration.

All symbols the test uses (nxsched_smp_call_single, nxsched_smp_call, OK, CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS, CPU_COUNT, sched_getaffinity, nxsem_reset, sem_* functions) are either named in the statement or existing NuttX APIs discoverable from the repository. The test's behavior (semaphore-based synchronization to verify callback execution) matches the described semantics.
